name: Citizenship by Descent / Birth

requirement_groups.name: Both parents citizens, or one parent citizen + born in country

requirements.blocker_text: Law on Citizenship, Article 4: a child acquires citizenship automatically when both parents are Macedonian citizens, or when one parent is a citizen and the child is born in North Macedonia. Adopted children are treated identically to biological children.

Article 5: a child born abroad to one Macedonian-citizen parent acquires citizenship if registered as a citizen before turning 18, or if the child becomes a permanent resident of North Macedonia before turning 18.
requirements.fix_path: Register the child as a Macedonian citizen with a consulate, or establish permanent residence in North Macedonia, before the child turns 18.

sources.title: Refworld (UNHCR-affiliated) -- hosted consolidated English text of North Macedonia's Law on Citizenship (2022 consolidation), Articles 2, 4-6 (birth/descent) and 7-11 (naturalization)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (North Macedonia). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to Refworld's hosted consolidated text, tier 2, not a North Macedonian government domain (Official Gazette) directly. GENUINE, GENDER-NEUTRAL FINDING: the law refers generically to 'parents' throughout Articles 4-6 with no father/mother asymmetry found -- consistent with Venezuela and Honduras built earlier in this dataset, and a contrast to Syria's and Guatemala's older gendered descent framing. Article 6 also grants citizenship to a child found or born in the country to unknown/stateless parents, lost only if a foreign parent is later identified before age 15 AND the child holds another nationality -- a real statelessness safeguard, disclosed as a distinctive feature. dual_citizenship_allowed set true per Article 2 (citizens may hold another state's citizenship) -- but see mk_citizenship_naturalisation.json's notes for the fuller, more conditional picture on renunciation requirements at naturalization.
